decisions.quote: Experimental Economics Replication Project Replication of Participation by Charness, G./Dufwenberg, M. (2011) in: The American Economic Review, 101(4), 1211–1237. Replication Authors: Teck Hua Ho, Hang Wu Charness and Dufwenberg test how communication can help achieve beneficial social outcomes in a hidden-information context depending on whether low-talent agents can participate in a Paretoimproving outcome or not. Communication is effective when low-talent agents can participate but not if they cannot participate. Hypothesis to bet on: Communication is effective in a hidden-information game when low-talent agents can participate in a Pareto-improving outcome (a comparison of the “Low B’s Don’t rate” for the messages (m) and no messages (nm) treatments for the (5,7) hidden information game).
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Charness and Dufwenberg (2011), p. 1/4 (line 1292)
decisions.reason: The main paper (Ref. 36, Table S1, Table S2) and the dedicated primary project replication report explicitly identify Charness and Dufwenberg (2011), 'Participation', American Economic Review 101(4), 1211–1237, as the re-tested original study. Both the shipped row and blind target 3 match this original paper.

decisions.quote: Discussion Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has been replicated at a significance level of α < 5%. The relative effect size equals 93.39% and the p-value of the hypothesis test is 0.003.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Charness and Dufwenberg (2011), Discussion, p. 3/4 (line 1292)
decisions.reason: In the individual primary replication report for Charness and Dufwenberg (2011), communication significantly increased low-talent B's Don't rate from 44.83% in the no-messages treatment to 80.56% in the messages treatment (p = 0.003, relative effect size 93.39%; A's In rate also significantly increased from 62.12% to 83.33%), and the Discussion states an explicit overall verdict that the hypothesis of interest was replicated at α < 5% (corroborated by 'Yes' in Table S1). Both shipped and blind codings are right.

decisions.quote: Sample The sample for replication consists of 264 students (132 participants in each treatment) at the National University of Singapore. There are no exclusion criteria. We use the material of the original experiment (paper and pencil). The materials are: index cards with identification numbers, a coin, an opaque bag, blank pieces of paper, decision sheets, pens to write messages and instructions. Procedure We follow the procedure of the original article, with only slight but unavoidable deviations as outlined below.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Charness and Dufwenberg (2011), Sample and Procedure, p. 1/4 (line 1292)
decisions.reason: The study collected new experimental data from a new sample of 264 students at the National University of Singapore to re-test the published finding of Charness and Dufwenberg (2011), which is a replication under the codebook.

corrected_value.title: The Potential of Social Identity for Equilibrium Selection

decisions.quote: Experimental Economics Replication Project Replication of The Potential of Social Identity for Equilibrium Selection by Chen, R./Chen, Y. (2011) in: The American Economic Review, 101(6), 2562–2589. Replication Authors: Teck Hua Ho, Hang Wu Chen and Chen study effort in a minimum effort game varying whether subjects have a salient ingroup or outgroup identity. They find that effort is higher for those with a salient ingroup identity. Hypothesis to bet on: Effort in a minimum effort game is higher for subjects with a salient ingroup identity than for subjects with a salient outgroup identity (a comparison of mean effort between the Enhanced Ingroup treatment and the Enhanced Outgroup treatment).
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Chen and Chen (2011), p. 1/4 (line 1297)
decisions.reason: The main paper (Ref. 37, Table S1, Table S2) and the dedicated primary project replication report explicitly identify Chen and Chen (2011), 'The Potential of Social Identity for Equilibrium Selection', American Economic Review 101(6), 2562–2589, as the re-tested original study. Both the shipped row and blind target 4 match this original paper.

decisions.quote: Discussion Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has not been replicated at a significance level of α < 5%. The relative effect size equals 21.82% and the p-value of the hypothesis test is 0.571.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Chen and Chen (2011), Discussion, p. 3/4 (line 1297)
decisions.reason: In the individual primary replication report for Chen and Chen (2011), the treatment effect on effort in the minimum-effort game between Enhanced Ingroup and Enhanced Outgroup was statistically nonsignificant (coefficient = 5.204, p = 0.571, relative effect size 21.82%), and the Discussion states an explicit overall verdict that the hypothesis of interest was not replicated at α < 5% and notes the 'lack of an ingroup favoritism effect in the replication study' (corroborated by 'No' in Table S1). Descriptive observations of effort time trends do not override the explicit overall replication verdict under Codebook Rule 1.

decisions.quote: Sample The sample for replication consists of 168 students (84 participants in each treatment) at the National University of Singapore. There are no exclusion criteria. Materials We use the material of the original experiment (programmed in z-Tree) along with the original instructions, both available on the journal’s webpage.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report for Chen and Chen (2011), Sample and Materials, p. 1/4 (line 1297)
decisions.reason: The study collected new experimental data from a new sample of 168 students at the National University of Singapore to re-test the published finding of Chen and Chen (2011), which is a replication under the codebook.
